title: Local finite-free tensor model
statement: For schemes Z,Y [def-pc-scheme], a closed immersion i:Z -> Y [def-weil-closed-immersion] with additive tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and a cochain complex P on Y [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], suppose a:P -> (i_*O_Z)[0] is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] and every term of P is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put T=i*P, the actual termwise tensor pullback. For any open V of Z and affine open U of Y whose immersion ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], put W=V intersect i^(-1)(U), regarded as an open of V. Restricting T to V and then to its over site W [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives a finite-free zero-differential model by a quasi-isomorphism roof [lem-sc-homology-evaluation-formal-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. No complex J or K-injectivity claim occurs in this statement.

source.place: Koszul complex and quotient zero-differential computation in the proof; Tag 068C for the finite-free resolution of a Koszul-regular quotient. Derived-resolution comparison supplies the tensor version.

proof.text: Choose m,f,hf,hreg from hU and use exists_koszul_projective_resolution to obtain an actual ProjectiveResolution Q of the quotient with Q.complex equal to the Koszul complex.

Apply exists_local_koszul_augmented_carrier to Q and hQ, obtaining K, its local augmentation b to the restriction of i_*O_Z, local K-flatness, and bounded finite-free zero-differential data for its restricted tensor pullback.

Restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms by preservation of finite limits and colimits. Apply isKFlat_restrict to the K-flatness component of hP. These give the restricted augmentation F(a) as a K-flat resolution of the same F(S) as b.

Apply exists_local_kflat_tensor_roof with augmentations F(a) and b to obtain L,q,p and both quasi-isomorphisms. Use G(K) as E and combine the roof with the zero differentials, bounds and finite-free bases from the carrier theorem. This is exactly HasFiniteFreeZeroModel.

lean.statement:
theorem local_tensor_has_finite_free_zero_model
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).Additive]
    (P : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ)
    (a : P ⟶ (HomologicalComplex.single Y.Modules (.up ℤ) 0).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)))
    (_hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := Y.sheaf) a)
    (_hflat : ∀ k : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (P.X k)) :
    let T := ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P
    ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (U : Y.affineOpens)
      (_hU : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
        Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f),
      HasFiniteFreeZeroModel
        (V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.over (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))
        ((moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor Z V (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))).obj T)
